Overview

Product designer with 15+ years across startups, research institutions, and independent practice. I care most about work that actually helps people — whether that means redesigning a complex data tool, building a brand from nothing, or writing the CSS myself when it gets to that point. Strong generalist with deep roots in product UX, design systems, and visual craft. Comfortable leading, comfortable contributing, genuinely uncomfortable with work that doesn't hold up.

Experience

Lead Product Designer

St. Jude Children's Research Hospital — St. Jude Cloud 2019 – 2025 · Remote, Memphis TN

St. Jude Cloud is a global genomics data platform — petabytes of childhood cancer research data made accessible to researchers and clinicians worldwide. I was the lead designer for six years, covering everything from day-to-day feature work to major platform overhauls.

Drove the full redesign of the platform's core experience, introduced a design system used across eight+ applications, and shipped a series of zero-to-one products that are now actively used by the research community. Worked directly with PMs, engineers, and research scientists — often as the first person to define what we were actually trying to build.

  • Led end-to-end redesign of St. Jude Cloud, a platform serving researchers at 300+ institutions
  • Built and maintained the platform design system, spanning components, patterns, and documentation
  • Designed the Visualization Community — a tool for creating and sharing interactive genomics research
  • Designed PeCan, a pediatric cancer knowledge base; went from a frustrating research tool to one of the most cited in the field
  • Managed a small design team; ran critique, mentored junior designers, and kept things moving without a lot of overhead

Design Director

NatureQuant 2019 – 2024 · Remote

First design hire at a nature-exposure health tech startup. I built the design function from scratch — brand identity, design system, two consumer apps, marketing site, and eventually a small team. The scientific credibility was there from day one; my job was to make the work feel as serious as the research behind it.

NatureDose was a mobile wellness app that helped people track and build nature habits against a research-backed dose target. NatureScore was a location-based index — essentially a walkability score for nature exposure. Both shipped. Both worked. I'm proud of the brand as much as the product work; we made something that looked genuinely different in a crowded wellness market.

  • Created the full visual identity and brand language for NatureQuant from zero
  • Designed and shipped NatureDose on iOS and Android — from concept through App Store launch
  • Designed NatureScore, a data-dense consumer product that had to feel approachable
  • Defined UX strategy and product roadmap alongside the CEO and engineering leads
  • Built and managed a small design team as the company grew

Product Designer

Oregon Center for Applied Science (ORCAS) 2007 – 2010 · Eugene & Seattle, OR

Designed consumer mobile apps and digital wellness tools — Moodhacker, Jauntly, and a series of CBT-based programs. Handled UI/UX, branding, and user research, and wrote front-end code for most of what I designed. Good early experience in moving fast and figuring out which corners are worth cutting.

Designer & Creative Director

Independent Practice 2008 – Present · Remote

Ongoing freelance practice running alongside everything else. Work has ranged from product design and data visualization to brand identity and front-end development. Clients have included Reuters, Stack Overflow, St. Jude Children's Hospital, REI Cooperative Action Fund, XPRIZE, Kirkus, Hoka One One, UGG, John Lewis, and a lot of smaller projects I find just as interesting.
